newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-RAPTORS SET TEAM THREE-POINT MARK IN ROUT OF SPURS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-RAPTORS SET TEAM THREE-POINT MARK IN ROUT OF SPURS.

text.p: Damon Stoudamire scored 21 points to lead six players in double figures and the Toronto Raptors established a team record for three-pointers in a 125-92 rout of the hapless San Antonio Spurs Wednesday.
The Raptors never trailed, posted a season high in points while knocking down 15 three-pointers.
Toronto snapped a five-game losing string with just their fourth road win in 24 away games this season.

"I was nervous about the game but we were determined to get a win on this road trip," said Raptors coach Darrell Walker. "Our club played really hard tonight. We got some easy shots and made some big threes."

Walt Williams scored 19 points and Carlos Rogers added 18 and nine rebounds for the Raptors, who shot 55 percent (49-of-89) from the field and 60 percent (15-of-25) from three-point range, while out-rebounding the Spurs 55-35.
"I have no sympathy for them," Williams said. "Last year, when I was with Sacramento, they kicked our butts all over the place."
Dominique Wilkins and Carl Herrera scored 17 points apiece for San Antonio, losers of five in a row.
The injury-riddled Spurs, who have been without star centre David Robinson for most of the season, have 39 losses in 51 games after losing just 43 games in the previous two seasons combined.
In Vancouver, Dean Garrett scored 25 points and the Minnesota Timberwolves held the Grizzlies to a mere seven points in the third quarter in a 84-73 victory.
Vancouver was outscored 30-7 in the third, shooting a franchise-low 13.3 percent (2-of-15) from the field as Minnesota used a 20-0 run to build a 22-point lead.
Kevin Garnett added 20 points and Tom Gugliotta had 20 and 10 rebounds for Minnesota, which climbed back to within one game of the .500 mark with the victory.
Shareef Abdur-Rahim led Vancouver with 26 points.
In Orlando, Penny Hardaway scored 21 points and Horace Grant added 20 and 10 rebounds as the Magic made a winner out of new coach Richie Adubato with a 95-84 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.
Adubato was making his debut as Orlando head coach after Brian Hill was fired Tuesday.

Orlando centre Rony Seikaly was ejected with 5:24 remaining after receiving two technicals for arguing with officials. But the Magic, who led 82-79 after Isaiah Rider made both free throws for Portland, went on an 8-0 run to put the game away.
In Atlanta, Mookie Blaylock scored 19 points to lead a balanced attack as the Hawks cruised to a 100-87 win over the Indiana Pacers for their 21st victory in their last 22 home games.
Dikembe Mutombo had 17 points and 10 rebounds and Christian Laettner added 16 points for Atlanta, which led by as many as 24 points.
Reggie Miller scored 19 points and Antonio Davis added 17 and 10 rebounds for the Pacers, who have lost four of their last five games.
In Charlotte, Glen Rice scored 36 points and tied club records for points in a quarter and half as the Hornets rallied to beat the Phoenix Suns 123-115.
Vlade Divac had 19 points and 11 rebounds and Anthony Mason added 19 and eight assists for Charlotte, who placed all five starters in double figures.
Rice scored 20 of his team's 41 points in the second quarter and had 28 in the first half for Charlotte. He also hit 6-of-8 shots from three-point range.
The Hornets trailed by seven points after three quarters but used a 37-point fourth quarter to rally for the win.
At Detroit, Lindsey Hunter scored 25 points and Grant Hill added 24, eight rebounds and seven assists to lead the Pistons to a 100-85 victory over the Washington Bullets.
Joe Dumars had 19 points and seven assists and Terry Mills recorded 15 points and nine rebounds for Detroit, winners of four in a row.
Juwan Howard had 25 points and 10 rebounds and Tracy Murray added 15 points for the Bullets, who fell to 2-3 under new coach Bernie Bickerstaff.
At Golden State, Latrell Sprewell poured in 41 points and Chris Mullin recorded a triple-double as the Warriors dealt the road-weary Boston Celtics their eighth straight loss, 112-101.
Mullin had 19 points, 12 rebounds, 10 assists and seven steals for his fifth career triple-double.
Todd Day scored 27 points and Eric Williams added 19 for the Celtics, who committed 27 turnovers in falling to 0-7 on their current nine-game road trip.
In Los Angeles, Terrell Brandon scored 19 of his 31 points in the fourth quarter and Tyrone Hill added 24 points and 12 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers trounced the Lakers 103-84.
Chris Mills scored 19 points and Bob Sura added 11 points, eight rebounds and six assists for the Cavaliers, who are 13-0 when reaching the 100-point mark this season.
Elden Campbell scored 23 points and Eddie Jones added 21 for the Lakers, who are forced to play without injured star centre Shaquille O'Neal for the next several weeks.
